requirements.title: One verified release identity
requirements.description: Bundle, native control-plane binaries, dependency closure and configuration schema are bound by one artifact-set digest with recorded provenance; mismatched CLI or tampered content is refused before extraction.

validation.notes: Two builds from equal pinned inputs yield one release digest (P10-A01); native binary reproducibility verified twice and recorded (reproducible on the reference host); configuration digest ignores locator and secrets; tampered bundle byte, native CLI sha mismatch, edited identity, wrong architecture (unsupported_capability naming the artifact), undeclared provenance policy, production signature verified through the release-authority seam, untrusted signer, tampered signed copy, unsigned development release refused in production, signer failure leaves no release; credential canary absent from every emitted file including bundle entries (P10-A06). Shared-seam evidence outside this scenario: packages/cloudrelease/cloudrelease_test.go (Canonical bytes and digest pinned; provenance and limits outside the identity; manifest shape refusals. Shared by internal/cloudtarget (target-side verify).)

Delivery copies the release-bound binary and verifies remote sha256sum before chmod; remote digest mismatch, wrong architecture, tampered local binary and a bundle outside a release are refused (P10-A02); no deploy-time compile path exists.
GC honours unexpired artifact leases of active and predecessor releases; unreadable leases refuse GC.
Connect ReleasesService build/get/verify with typed error details.

REST build/get/verify; tampered binary yields 422 release_verification_failed naming the check. Shared-seam evidence outside this scenario: internal/cloudtarget/cloudtarget_test.go (Target-side verify over the same manifest (P08 evidence).)

requirements.title: Safe bounded extraction into owned staging
requirements.description: Archive traversal, escaping symlinks, absolute paths, oversized expansion and incomplete stages are rejected; the active release is never modified before a candidate is validated.

validation.notes: Traversal, absolute path, escaping symlink, device entry, entry-count bomb, oversized entry and oversized expansion archives are refused through the release's declared limits before any write; the store tree is byte-identical after verification (P10-A04). An incomplete stage (no .complete) is refused by Verify, Store.Load and the delivery resolver (P10-A05). Shared-seam evidence outside this scenario: packages/binaryfetch/archive_bounded_test.go (Bounded walker refusals shared by cloud verify and target stage.)

requirements.title: Explicit activation with retained predecessor
requirements.description: Activation commits runtime and edge state with recoverable ordering, records old and new release identities, retains a compatible predecessor and reports rollback eligibility.

validation.notes: [REQ:STC-P0-028] Every fixture x scope executes through typed target verbs with the operation id and fence (no shell syntax reaches reach.Command.Args: reach.ValidateCommand over every dispatched call); activation ordering stage -> recovery point -> runtime -> pointer -> route; crashes before the verb, after the verb and inside the target between runtime and pointer are reconciled by a successor attempt to the candidate with the predecessor retained and one pointer commit; seeded data survives an update and a failed activation; two deployments sharing postgres keep the resource when one is retired; legacy conversion binds recorded mappings first and never deletes unmapped directories; a start uses the active pointer and refuses an interrupted activation. Shared-seam evidence outside this scenario: internal/cloudtarget/persistent_data_test.go (target owner adopts legacy data by rename into persistent-data/<binding>, links the release tree, leaves unmapped directories untouched, pins ports as environment, --restart keeps the predecessor) and internal/cli/cloudtargethandlers/argv_flags_test.go (b64 JSON flag spelling, activate flags).

[REQ:STC-P0-028] workload.stop is one scoped lifecycle stop (privilegebroker process.stop.scoped) without process patterns or ports; retirement runs route -> runtime -> grants -> data -> artifacts, refuses an irreversible data disposition without a target owner, and reports active/previous artifacts as retained.

[REQ:STC-P0-027] Delivery negotiates the platform, places bundle + release manifest + native control plane through reach.Deliver with the manifest digest, refuses a platform mismatch before any byte moves and a bare bundle before staging; a Bridge-bound target gets a typed reach_unavailable instead of an SSH fallback.

[REQ:STC-P0-028] Desired vs observed reconciliation with separate revision/timestamps; intentional stop never restarted; drift corrections are plan-scoped proposals; reboot policy follows declared supervision; retirement plan lists retained/deleted objects in owner order and blocks without an explicit data policy; cleanup protection is reference-based (stale leases do not expose active, previous or recovery-referenced artifacts).

[REQ:STC-P0-028] GET/PUT desired-state contract (observation_may_restart, reboot policy), POST reconcile proposes then admits only the reviewed digest through the operation owner, retire/plan and retire/apply, data-bindings inventory (read-only) and adopt (declared bindings only, no data moved, mapping reaches the next plan).
Strategies, declared downtime, rollback eligibility, retirement order, desired-state contract for vrooli-autoheal, protected cleanup.
